payload.title: Main-checkout lock: retro-loop/cleanup-loop paralyzes concurrent take/pick/approve because…
payload.description:
Main-checkout lock: retro-loop/cleanup-loop paralyzes concurrent take/pick/approve because per-item commits never release .fgos/main-checkout.lock between items, and approve has no retry-on-lock-held unlike take/pick.

Root cause (confirmed via code trace, not speculation):
- fgos-coding-compounding (retro-loop) and cleanup-next write directly to the main checkout (no worktree -- the item's own fgw/<id> branch is already merged/torn down by this stage). Each commit fires the pre-commit hook, which acquires the STR65 main-checkout lock file (guard against two writers racing one shared git index). The hook never proactively releases it -- HOOK_TTL_MS=20s self-expiry only (src/runner/main-checkout-lock.mjs:131), by design.
- The session identity is stable across the whole loop run (resolveWriterIdentity reads CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/FGOS_SESSION_ID from env -- confirmed in src/util/session-identity.mjs), so self-recognition (D6) means the loop never blocks itself -- but the lock stays continuously "hot" for the ENTIRE sweep duration (up to 15 items per retro-loop run), refusing every OTHER session's take/pick/approve for that whole time.
- take/pick already retry-with-backoff on lock-held via withLockRetry (src/runner/lock-wait.mjs, tsk-6c2/tsk-2rf) -- bin/fgos.mjs:2966,3039. approve does NOT (bin/fgos.mjs:3426 calls approveUseCase -> mergeRunnerItem directly, hard-fails immediately on lock-held) -- an unexplained asymmetry, even though merge.mjs's own lock-held error shape is already withLockRetry-compatible (see comment at src/runner/merge.mjs:748).
- Critically: an already-proven fix pattern for this exact class of problem EXISTS and is already shipped, just not applied everywhere it's needed. bin/fgos.mjs:3373 and :3402 (case 'return', tsk-45z) already call releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn(dir, resolveWriterIdentity(dir).id) right at a main-sourced item's own natural settling point (verify passed -> awaiting-approval, or verify failed -> blocked) -- releasing this session's own lock early instead of leaving the next writer to wait out the TTL. case 'compound' (bin/fgos.mjs:1589-1628, the terminal per-item step of the retro pipeline) and case 'cleanup' (bin/fgos.mjs:1515-1565, the terminal per-item step of the cleanup pipeline) have no equivalent release call, despite being exactly the same shape of "main-sourced item reaches its own settling point."

Proposed fix (mirrors the proven tsk-45z pattern, no new abstraction, no hook/TTL/contract changes):
1. case 'compound' (bin/fgos.mjs): call releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn(dir, resolveWriterIdentity(dir).id) right after addOutcome records the docType/docPath tag (~line 1626), before returning -- same call, same placement logic as tsk-45z's return case.
2. case 'cleanup' (bin/fgos.mjs): same release call at both its settling points -- the moveWork(...to:'blocked') branch (~line 1547) and the moveWork(...to:'done') branch (~line 1563).
3. Wire approve (bin/fgos.mjs:3426, and check sync-root/promote-to-component which share mergeRunnerItem-style merge paths) through withLockRetry the same way take/pick already are (bin/fgos.mjs:2966,3039 pattern) -- closing the asymmetry where approve alone hard-fails immediately on lock-held with no retry.

Explicitly rejected alternatives (already evaluated, do not re-litigate without new evidence): batching multiple items into one commit (breaks the per-item commit-as-audit-trail contract, no gain on the final commit's own contention window); giving retro/cleanup items their own throwaway worktree (highest cost, the land-to-main step still needs the same lock briefly, buys little over the release-early fix); narrower per-path locking (unsound -- STR65 protects the single shared git index per checkout, which is not divisible by path).

Context for whoever picks this up: this closes a real, reproduced operational pain (main checkout completely unavailable to any other session's take/pick/approve for the full duration of a retro-loop/cleanup-loop sweep), not a hypothetical. Safety-critical surface (STR65 lock) -- implementation must preserve the identity-checked, TOCTOU-safe release discipline releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn already has; this is purely about calling it from two more already-existing settling points, not touching its own internals.
